_comment: The evaluation set. Replace these cases with your own.
Each case needs a projectId, a question, and what SHOULD come back.
Say it with expectedText: a short, distinctive phrase quoted off the sheet
that answers the question. A case passes when a retrieved chunk contains it.
Matching ignores case and collapses whitespace, so a phrase broken across a
line in the PDF still matches. Give an array to accept any of several.
Prefer text over expectedPages. A combined page number is DERIVED from
document order: re-upload the same PDFs in another order and every page
number in this file quietly points at a different sheet, while the run still
prints a number. That is how this set previously reported recall of 40% and
20% for two retrieval configurations that were both returning the right
chunk at rank 1 — the page numbers had been written from the source PDFs'
filenames rather than the app's combined numbering. The words on a sheet do
not move. Expectations are now checked against the corpus before the run,
so one that can never match stops the run instead of scoring as a miss.
Build a case with:
node benchmarks/retrieval_eval.mjs --capture "your question" --project <id>
It prints the top hits with their text, so you quote what is really there.
Aim for 30-50 cases and TAG them by class. The tag breakdown is the useful
part: an average hides that identifier lookups went from 40% to 95% while
open questions went slightly backwards, and that is exactly the trade a
retrieval change makes. Keep roughly ten of each.
Include failures you have actually seen. A set of questions you already know
work measures nothing.

question: What building code is specified for this project, and what should be followed when the drawings reference the latest edition or other standards?
note: General structural notes: the governing code and the requirement to follow referenced standards / latest applicable editions.

question: What is the typical top of footing elevation shown on the foundation plan?
note: Foundation plan elevation lookup. Typical top of footing is -13'-4", UNO.

question: What are the thickness and reinforcement requirements for the typical slab-on-grade?
note: Foundation plan slab-on-grade note: 4-inch slab with 4x4-W2.9xW2.9 WWR at mid-depth on vapor retarder over prepared subgrade. The WWR designation is the distinctive token; the word 'slab' is everywhere.

question: At what maximum spacing are control joints required in the slab-on-grade?
note: Maximum spacing is 10'-8" OC, with joints at each column grid. Anchored on the phrase rather than the dimension because feet-and-inches marks vary between straight and typographic quotes in extracted text.

question: What is the specified floor construction at Level 1, including concrete thickness, steel deck size, total depth, and reinforcement location?
note: Level 1 framing plan: 3 1/2-inch normal-weight concrete on 3-inch 20GA composite steel deck, total depth 6 1/2 inches, 6x6-W2.1xW2.1 WWR 1 1/2 inches below top of slab.

question: What is the maximum permitted deck span at Level 1?
note: Level 1 framing plan specifies a maximum deck span of 11'-0".

question: What temporary bracing is required for the steel columns at Level 2 before the wood stud walls are erected?
note: Level 2 framing notes: steel columns are unstable without the wood stud walls, so the contractor provides temporary bracing before those walls are erected.

question: What does the abbreviation "HSS" mean in the structural drawings?
note: Abbreviation lookup in the general notes. Anchored on the expansion, not on 'HSS', which appears in member callouts all over the set and would pass on any sheet.

question: For Special Inspections, what items are included under IT-2 Steel Construction?
note: Special inspections schedule. This anchor is verbatim — confirmed present in the retrieved chunk text. Previously marked expectedPages [8], which is a filename number; the content is on combined pages 4 and 5.

question: For IT-3 Concrete Construction, what inspections are required for reinforcement, cast-in anchors, and post-installed anchors?
note: IT-3 covers reinforcement/prestressing, rebar welding, cast-in anchors and post-installed adhesive/mechanical anchors. The bare 'IT-3' fallback is looser than the heading and will also match a cross-reference.
